text: The main problem is that a lot of mixed, unsegregated waste ends up in India's landfills, so most urban dumps are overflowing open sites rather than scientifically designed landfills. Decaying organic waste releases methane, which causes frequent fires, and leachate mixes into groundwater, affecting the health of nearby residents. Effective solutions start at the source by segregating waste into wet, dry, and hazardous, as required by the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016. Wet waste can be turned into compost or biogas, dry waste can be recycled, and old dumps can be cleared through biomining. Community participation is very important: awareness campaigns like the Swachh Bharat Mission change household habits and make segregation and recycling practically successful.
